newsitem.title: UK: Fred West film plan angers British MPs, relatives.
newsitem.headline: Fred West film plan angers British MPs, relatives.

text.p: Churchmen and politicians on Tuesday condemned plans for a movie about the life of Fred and Rosemary West, the British couple who killed a series of women and girls to satisfy perverted sexual cravings.
"The whole idea of a film about the Wests appals me," said David Bentley, the Bishop of Gloucester, the west of England city made notorious by the events at 25 Cromwell Street.
News of the plan came just a day less than two years after Fred West was found hanged in a prison cell where he was awaiting multiple charges of murder.

Legal official Peter Harris confirmed reports that the London-based Portman Entertainment Group had acquired an option to make the movie about West and his wife, who is currently serving a life sentence for 10 murders.
The option includes access to tape recordings of police interviews with West, tapes of his favourite blue movies and pages of his memoirs written when awaiting trial.
Gloucester member of parliament Douglas French said: "The showing of any film will be deeply painful for relatives of victims and an insult to their...wish to grieve in private."
Fred West's older brother Doug joined the condemnation. "The relatives of the victims have had enough. I have had enough... it's a bit sick as far as I am concerned," he told BBC radio.
